svg.title: The Sema ceremony of the Mevlevi order
svg.desc: Diagram: a turning dervish (semazen) with labelled hat, skirt and hand positions, a top view of the hall showing dervishes turning anticlockwise around the sheikh's sheepskin, and a seven-step sequence of the ceremony.
svg.text: The Sema: Turning as Prayer in the Mevlevi Tradition
The ceremony of the Mawlawi order, founded by Rumi's followers after his death in 1273
The black cloak (hirka) is shed before turning, a sign of leaving worldly ties.
Top view of the sema hall
Each dervish turns on his own axis while moving
around the hall, like planets around a sun.
The sema is a form of dhikr (remembrance of God): a prayer ritual, not a performance. UNESCO inscribed it as intangible heritage in 2008.
